title: Imperial Serenaders: Albert Snaer, personnel and tailgate rivalry
summary: He describes the Imperial Serenaders, Albert Snaer's wild trumpet, the full line-up, tailgate wagon contests with Kid Rena, and the Camellia band with George Stewart.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, who were the Imperial Serenaders you mentioned then?
Oh, well, who was in charge of that when the first started was, you might recall, you might notice boys, Albert Snyder, you might heard of him.
He's still playing. He played with the Carl Hopkins band out of New York. I believe he was playing in California with Dixieland. No, is he?
No, in New York. In New York. In New York? I think he lives in Connecticut. Well, he's in Connecticut.

He was in Connecticut. But I believe he joined his daughter in California. I thought he was in California. His son, his daughter, California. He was a fine trumpet player. He worked out here on Steamer Capital for years. He was one of these wild, wild trumpet players. We used to tie these wagons up on Sunday evening, Kid Rene and our band Imperial Serenaders, put them tailgates together, you know? And these go on to buck one another. They always come out these cans of beer from these ballrooms and get them some beer and stuff like that. Yeah.
They have a clarinet player with the Imperial Serenaders? A saxophone?

Well, we had a saxophone and clarinet player. We had a trombone with Raymond Brown. You heard of Raymond Brown? Mm-hmm. And I was on the drums, Albert Snoyer was on the trumpet, and George Augustin playing banjo. He's in California now. His dad was the president of the local years back before he passed. And Wilhelmina Barth, you heard of Wilhelmina Barth? Yeah. He was playing piano at the time. Let me see, that's, I can recall. And we had a Jeruzan, a saxophone player. He's in California now. Bass was, bass player, old man by the name of Gus. Did you ever hear August used to call him?
I can't play, Sam. I guess I've heard of him.

Yeah. I'll forget his name. Lucian used to play with him. My brother Lucian played with him too. And I'll say, I play with the Chamelea band too. Whose band was that? That's Janet Ferdahls and George Stewart, the clarinet player. George Stewart, yeah. George Stewart, yeah.
You don't hear too much about him. Whatever happened to him? He died. He's one of the old ones, yeah. He was an elderly fellow?
Oh yeah, sure. About how long ago did he die? George Stewart, yeah.
I'd sooner say the thirties. In the twenties or thirties.
In the twenties or thirties. That's when he died.
That's right. How did George Stewart play?
What style? Any particular style? Did he read music much? No, I don't believe it was much of a reader. Did he have a good clarinet player with the…
Fine clarinet player. I didn't mean to interrupt you. Go ahead and say that. He was a fine clarinet player though.
He was a fine clarinet player though. He was a steward.

I don't know the trumpet players or something like that. I can recall the old man who was a bass player. the bass player, Johnny Prodoss and George Stude. And Albert Walters said he played with them, trumpet player Albert Fernandez and he'll play with us now. He said he worked with them.
